doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Jazz parties and an aging audience
summary: Discussion of jazz party audiences getting older and an unsuccessful kids band booking.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah that’s a really interesting phenomenon, the jazz parties. I wonder if you see, are the audiences maintaining themselves?

Pretty good. Pretty good. It’s the aging audience is a problem that I don’t think any of us know quite how to deal with it. I mean we all would love to get all the kids involved but we know it’s probably not going to happen maybe in our lifetime. And you go places and here’s an example. I think we played down in Vero Beach with my 8-piece group you know. My 8-piece band, we’ll start from playing “The Chant” and go all the way up to playing “Love for Sale” by Buddy Rich. Stuff like that. Try to expand their horizons a little bit. But they had an all-star kids band there and we were going to follow them as the act that day. They played their song and left. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
I know. “Wait, there’s something for you here to listen to.”

I’m thinking what! And we had a few choice words to say. But it’s a sad thing. But the jazz party group is elderly, because jazz parties by virtue of the people they have to bring in, it’s very expensive.
